To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the KM-function in connection with the Bayesian method of parameter estimation is a good candidate for the modelling and prediction of growth of organisms, (ii) it is a useful alternative to classical growth functions, (iii) it is especially useful for the modelling of growth with inflexion, which occurs in many organisms.
the KM-function can be used for short-term prediction of time-determinate sigmoid growth and its prediction accuracy is comparable to classical growth functions.

the KM-function is a model of asymmetric sigmoid time-determinate organism growth, that can be used for realistic growth prediction, and that its parameterisation by the Bayesian method is more accurate than parameterisation by the NLS method.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new sigmoid time-determinate model of plant growth and with the evaluation of its prediction accuracy.
the properties and short-term predictive accuracy of the KM-function, a mathematical model of sigmoid growth with finite growth period, finite lifespan and inflexion point at any age.
the theoretical analysis, empirical evaluation and application of the KM-function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the choice of a growth function should depend on the purpose of the study, the quality and length of the data series, and on the type of growth trajectory.
the KM-function is a good candidate for the modelling of sigmoid growth trajectories in forestry and other fields.
all four functions analysed in this study can be recommended for modelling of S-shape growth trajectories.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the KM-function is a promising alternative for growth modelling in forestry.
the KM-function is a good candidate for modelling of growth trajectories in organisms with finite life span.

the KM-function is a good candidate for modelling of sigmoid time-deterministic growth, especially when it is necessary to consider the asymmetry of growth curve and the expected lifespan of organism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the KM-function can be used for short-term prediction of growth of tree stems and other organisms with sigmoid growth trajectories.
the KM-function is a promising tool for modelling of time-determinate, asymmetrical sigmoid growth trajectories.
the KM-function can be used in growth analysis of organisms with a finite length of growth period and can be recommended for modelling of growth curves of asymmetrical sigmoidal shape.
